messages.subject: Editing stanfit graphs
parts:
Hi,

I am new to Stan and somewhat new to R. I would like to edit the graphs, so that instead of the number in brackets I have real label names.
My data includes the real names as well as the ID shown in the figures below, the ones I would like to change. Thank you very much for your help.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Editing stanfit graphs
parts:
Hi Tobias, there are two options that come to mind. (1) edit the ggplot object returned by traceplot() or (2) modify the parameter names in the stanfit object and then create the traceplot. I'll use the "eight_schools" Stan demo as an example. 

stanfit <- stan_demo("eight_schools")
trace <- traceplot(stanfit)

1) The labels you want to change are taken from the "parameter" factor variable in the "data" slot of the object. To see what they currently are use

print(levels(trace$data$parameter))

and to change them you can use the replacement form of the levels() function: 

levels(trace$data$parameter)[1] <- "new name" # change only the first

levels(trace$data$parameter) <- new_names # change all names, if new_names is character vector of correct length

plot(trace) # check the modified plot


2) To change the names in the stanfit object you can use the names method for stanfit objects. You can see what they currently are with 

print(names(stanfit))

 "mu"       "theta[1]" "theta[2]" "theta[3]" "theta[4]" "theta[5]"
 "theta[6]" "theta[7]" "theta[8]" "tau"      "lp__"  

and then you can replace as many of them as you want

names(stanfit)[1] <- "not_mu_anymore"
print(names(stanfit))

 "not_mu_anymore" "theta[1]"       "theta[2]"       "theta[3]"      
 "theta[4]"       "theta[5]"       "theta[6]"       "theta[7]"      
 "theta[8]"       "tau"            "lp__"      

Then when you create the traceplot it should use the new names. 

Hope that helps, 

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Editing stanfit graphs
parts:
Oh, I think my way works for the trace plot but not for the default plot of point estimates and intervals. That's because the ggplot objects for those plots have slightly different structures. Anyway, I think the second method I mentioned in my previous post (using the names method for stanfit objects to set parameter names) should still work (and should work for most if not all of the plots). 

There's also another way, but it only works for this type of plot (and not, for instance, trace plots), which is

Figure1 + scale_y_continuous(labels = letters[1:8], breaks = 1:8)

where I'm just using R's letters vector as a placeholder. If there are p parameters in the plot then you would set labels to a character vector of length p and set breaks = 1:p. 

Jonah
